title: The fix that made the errors go away
role: You own the Terraform for an AWS estate in several regions. The root module calls one child module per region and hands each one an aliased provider.

source.label: HashiCorp Discuss: Terraform catch-22, default provider vs per-region providers (January 2024)

brief: You are bringing existing resources under Terraform, region by region. The root module defines only aliased providers such as `aws.eu_west_1`, with no default one, and every module call passes `providers = { aws = aws.<region> }`. `terraform plan` fails before it starts.

steps.evidence:
$ terraform plan
│ Error: Invalid provider configuration
│ Provider "registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws" requires explicit configuration.
│ Add a provider block to the root module and configure the provider's
│ required arguments as described in the provider documentation.
│ Error: Invalid AWS Region:

choices.text: Find what still uses the default provider: run `terraform providers` and read each resource and module call
choices.why: If Terraform wants a default `aws`, something in the configuration is still linked to it: a resource without `provider`, or a module call without a `providers` mapping.

choices.text: Add a default `provider "aws"` block with any region so the error stops
choices.why: The error goes away, and so does your signal. Whatever was unlinked now quietly talks to that one region.
This isn't a plugin cache problem. Init succeeds and the plan fails the same way.

steps.situation: A colleague already added a default provider in us-east-1. The plan now runs without errors.
steps.evidence:
$ terraform plan -out=tf.plan | grep -E 'will be|Plan:'
  # module.eu_west_1.aws_s3_bucket.logs will be created
  # module.ap_south_1.aws_instance.app will be created
Plan: 37 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.

choices.text: Stop: resources you just imported shouldn't be created, so check which region each module really uses
choices.why: Imported resources should be no-ops. Creates mean the regional modules are looking in the default region and can't see their own resources.
You'd build a duplicate copy of your estate in the default region.

choices.text: Apply only one module with `-target` to see what happens
choices.why: An experiment on production that still creates real resources in the wrong place.

steps.situation: Someone suggests opening `terraform.tfstate` and writing the right region into each resource's provider string.

choices.text: Leave state alone: put an explicit `provider = aws.<region>` on the resources in each regional module
choices.why: Configuration decides which provider manages a resource; state only remembers it for resources removed from the configuration. In the thread, explicit per-resource providers were what finally worked.

choices.text: Hand-edit the provider strings in state
choices.why: The author tried it. Terraform then complained that a removed provider configuration was still needed, and later "Provider configuration not present".

choices.text: `terraform state rm` everything and import it all again
choices.why: Hours of work, and if the configuration is still wired to the default you import into the wrong region again.

steps.situation: Providers are fixed. The new plan shows destroys you didn't expect.

choices.text: Back up state, review each destroy, and keep fixing until the plan only does what you intend
choices.why: A plan is a promise. Apply only a saved plan you've read, and keep `terraform state pull` output so you can undo a mistake.

choices.text: Apply; the destroys are probably leftovers
choices.why: "Probably" on a destroy plan is how production databases disappear.

choices.text: Add `prevent_destroy` to the important resources first
choices.why: A sensible guard: apply fails instead of deleting. You still have to understand why Terraform wants to destroy them.

debrief.what_happened: On 25 January 2024 a user posted on HashiCorp Discuss (Terraform 1.7.1 and 1.6.0, AWS provider 5.31.0). The root module defined only per-region aliased AWS providers and called one child module per region with `providers = { aws = aws.<region> }`; the resources inside had no `provider` argument, and existing infrastructure was being imported with Terracognita. With no default provider, plan failed with "Invalid provider configuration" and "Invalid AWS Region". Adding a default made the errors vanish, but every regional module silently used the default's region. Editing `terraform.tfstate` produced an error that a removed provider configuration was still needed, and later attempts gave "Provider configuration not present". apparentlymart explained that configuration, not state, decides which provider a resource uses, so something in the configuration must still point at the default, and that `terraform providers` can show what. The author confirmed that an explicit per-region provider on every resource in every regional module fixed it, after which the plan showed destroys to sort out.
lessons: An error that disappears after a quick fix may have moved somewhere quieter.
Configuration decides the provider; don't edit state by hand to change it.
After an import, the plan should be a no-op; creates or destroys mean something is wired wrong.
Apply only a saved plan you have read, with a state backup.
